results.name: Adductor Stretch Side Standing
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart while keeping your hands together in front of your chest.
Take a step to the left while keeping your right foot in place.
Bend the left knee unless your right thigh becomes parallel to the floor.
Hold for a few seconds, return to the initial position, and repeat.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch.
Ensure your bent knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on your knee joint.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
results.description: Adductor Stretch Side Standing is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes.

results.name: Adductor Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with both legs extended upwards.
Open your legs wide apart, stretching your inner thighs.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, or as needed.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the stretch.
Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern, inhaling deeply through your nose and exhaling through your mouth while holding the stretch.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
results.description: Adductor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

results.name: All Fours Quad Stretch
instructions: Start in an all-fours position on a mat, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Reach back with your right hand to grasp the ankle of your right leg.
Gently pull your ankle towards your glutes, stretching your quadriceps, and hold the stretch in this position for 20-30 seconds.
Release your ankle and switch sides, repeating the stretch.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch.
Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine to protect your lower back.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
results.description: All Fours Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Armless Prayer Stretch
instructions: Begin on your knees, spread wide and feet touching, with your elbows on the floor, directly under your shoulders.
Place your hands on your shoulders, with your head positioned between your elbows close to the floor.
Gently lower your chest towards the floor, keeping your hips over your knees and your back straight.
Hold the stretch briefly, then return to the starting position. Repeat the movement.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your lower back throughout the exercise.
Focus on lowering your chest towards the floor to maximize the stretch in your shoulders and upper back.
Keep the stretch at least between 15-20 seconds to make the most out of it.
results.description: Armless Prayer Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Chest.

results.name: Arms Behind Back Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and clasp your hands behind your lower back.
Lift your chest up while rolling your shoulders back and downward.
Hold the stretch while breathing steadily.
tips: Maintain an upright posture without arching your lower back excessively.
Breathe slowly and deeply throughout the stretch, keeping your chest up.
Stretch only until you feel gentle tension, not pain.
Keep your neck relaxed and your head in a neutral position.
results.description: Arms Behind Back Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Arms Wide Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and extend your arms straight out to your sides at shoulder height.
Rotate your arms so that your palms face forward.
Move both your arms backward, as for as you can.
Hold the stretch for 20 - 30seconds, while breathing steadily.
tips: Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Stretch only until you feel mild tension in your chest, not pain.
Breathe slowly and rhythmically, focusing on the stretch.
results.description: Arms Wide Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Arms, Upper Back.

results.name: Back Slaps Wrap Around Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms out to the sides, keeping them lightly bent.
Cross your arms in front of your body, wrapping them around yourself as if giving yourself a hug.
Continue the swinging motion, alternating which arm crosses on top with each repetition.
tips: Keep your movements fluid to promote relaxation and prevent stiffness.
Focus on extending your arms fully to each side to maximize the stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure you are not rushing through the movement and to allow a thorough stretch.
results.description: Back Slaps Wrap Around Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Arms.

results.name: Back and Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Sit on a block with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart and raise your right arm overhead.
Bend your right elbow and reach down your back. Use your left hand to gently pull on your right elbow, enhancing the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Switch arms and repeat the stretch on the left side.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and proper posture throughout the stretch.
Avoid pulling too hard on your elbow; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Back and Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats.

results.name: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your head in a neutral position.
Tilt your head backward, stretching the front of your neck.
Return to the neutral position, then tilt your head forward to stretch the back of your neck.
Turn your head to one side, holding briefly, and then return to the neutral position. Repeat on the other side.
tips: Perform the movements slowly and gently to avoid straining your neck muscles.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down to prevent tension in your upper back and shoulders.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
results.description: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Band Warm Up Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the resistance band with both hands in front of you. Your arms should be straight, and hands shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lift the band overhead while slightly spreading your hands to stretch the band.
Hold this position for a few seconds and slowly return to the starting position with the band in front of you.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight but not locked to avoid joint strain.
Ensure the resistance band has appropriate tension to provide an effective stretch without causing discomfort.
Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
results.description: Band Warm Up Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
